# SLIM: Structured Low-bandwidth Information Markup (SLIM spec)

This repository defines **SLIM**, a minimal, text-first HTML authoring profile for delivering reliable, accessible information in low-bandwidth and austere network conditions.

Use these resources (in this order) when building or validating SLIM-compliant output.

---

## Canonical sources (read these first)

1) SLIM spec repository (source + context)
- https://github.com/cqueern/slim-spec

2) Bikeshed source of the specification (normative source of truth)
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cqueern/slim-spec/main/spec.bs

3) Latest release (built artifacts + version context)
- https://github.com/cqueern/slim-spec/releases/latest

4) Citable snapshot (Zenodo DOI)
- https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.16790879

If there is any ambiguity, treat `spec.bs` as authoritative.

---

## Quick “how to comply” (implementation-oriented summary)

When generating SLIM HTML, follow these high-level requirements.

### Content model
- Text-first, resilient delivery.
- Prefer semantic HTML with clear heading structure.
- Design for meaningful rendering without progressive enhancement.

### Network / transport requirements

SLIM is transport-aware but resilience-first.

- SLIM content MUST be served over HTTPS.
- When served over a network, servers SHOULD use a modern HTTP version that improves performance and resilience:

  - HTTP/3 — SHOULD be preferred where supported by both server and client.
  - HTTP/2 — SHOULD be used as a fallback where HTTP/3 is not available.
  - HTTP/1.1 — MAY be used only when HTTP/3 and HTTP/2 are unavailable.

- SLIM content MUST remain fully functional over HTTPS using HTTP/1.1.
- Protocol optimization MUST NOT be required for correctness.

### Single-request render goal
- Pages should render meaningfully from a single HTTPS request.
- Avoid external subresource dependencies.
- Prefer links over embedded assets.

### Scripts / tracking / third parties
- No JavaScript.
- No analytics, tracking pixels, or beacons.
- No embedded contexts (iframe, object, embed).
- No third-party fonts.
- No external stylesheets.

### Styling
- Inline styles are allowed only for a limited set of properties.
- Avoid layout-driven CSS.
- Color must not be the sole method of conveying meaning (accessibility).

### Forms / tables
- Tables and forms are discouraged and SHOULD be avoided unless clearly justified.
- If used, keep simple and robust.
- Do not rely on client-side validation.

### Mandatory authoring constraints
- All `<input>` elements MUST include a `type` attribute.
- Include the SLIM profile meta tag:
  - `<meta name="slim-profile" content="SLIM v1.0">`

## Suggested usage for AI coding agents

If writing a generator, linter, sanitizer, or validator:

1) Fetch and read:
   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cqueern/slim-spec/main/spec.bs

2) Extract normative rules (MUST / MUST NOT / SHOULD / MAY).

3) Enforce at minimum:
   - No scripts or tracking
   - No external CSS or third-party fonts
   - No embedded contexts
   - Required `<meta name="slim-profile" content="SLIM v1.0">`
   - `<input>` elements MUST include `type`
   - Page must not require additional network fetches for correctness
   - Transport optimization (HTTP/3 → HTTP/2 → HTTP/1.1) should not affect correctness

4) Prefer strict interpretation when uncertain.
